#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: scripts/lib/timeout-cmd.sh — shared _acceptance_timeout_prefix helper (#1752)
#   SPEC-1:  gtimeout-only PATH populates _ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[0]=gtimeout
#   SPEC-2:  no timeout binary leaves _ACCEPTANCE_TOUT empty, returns 0
#   SPEC-3:  build false-completion guard detects inert_build after helper is shared
#   SPEC-8:  structural grep — converted files call _acceptance_timeout_prefix, no command -v gtimeout
#   SPEC-9:  each of the five non-acceptance-gate sites produces gtimeout on gtimeout-only host
#   SPEC-10: per-caller kill-grace env bridge wired for run-tests.sh and run-mutation.sh
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "timeout-cmd.sh — shared _acceptance_timeout_prefix helper (#1752)"
setup_test_env "timeout-cmd-helper"
_test_cleanup_hook() { cleanup_test_env; }

# ── [#1752/SPEC-8]: structural grep — each converted file uses the helper ────
print_test_section "[#1752/SPEC-8] converted files contain _acceptance_timeout_prefix, no command -v gtimeout"

_s8_files=(
    "core/router/route.sh"
    "scripts/run-tests.sh"
    "scripts/run-mutation.sh"
    "scripts/lib/gh-automation.sh"
    "scripts/lib/acceptance-block.sh"
)
for _s8f in "${_s8_files[@]}"; do
    _s8path="$REPO_ROOT/$_s8f"
    if grep -q "_acceptance_timeout_prefix" "$_s8path" 2>/dev/null; then
        assert_pass "[#1752/SPEC-8] $_s8f: contains _acceptance_timeout_prefix"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1752/SPEC-8] $_s8f: contains _acceptance_timeout_prefix" \
            "missing call to shared helper in $_s8f"
    fi
    if ! grep -q "command -v gtimeout" "$_s8path" 2>/dev/null; then
        assert_pass "[#1752/SPEC-8] $_s8f: no command -v gtimeout inline pattern"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1752/SPEC-8] $_s8f: no command -v gtimeout inline pattern" \
            "old inline probe still present in $_s8f"
    fi
done

# ── Source the new shared helper — fails before the change ────────────────────
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/timeout-cmd.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/timeout-cmd.sh"

# ── Fake gtimeout: always exits 0 so the -k probe succeeds ───────────────────
mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/fakebin"
cat > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/fakebin/gtimeout" <<'FAKE_EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
exit 0
FAKE_EOF
chmod +x "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/fakebin/gtimeout"

_SAVED_PATH="$PATH"

# ── [#1752/SPEC-1]: gtimeout-only PATH populates _ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[0]=gtimeout ─
print_test_section "[#1752/SPEC-1] gtimeout-only PATH uses gtimeout as the binary"

_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT=()
unset _ACCEPTANCE_TIMEOUT_KILL_OK
export PATH="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/fakebin"
_acceptance_timeout_prefix 30
export PATH="$_SAVED_PATH"

if [[ "${#_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[@]}" -gt 0 ]]; then
    assert_eq "[#1752/SPEC-1] _ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[0] is gtimeout on gtimeout-only PATH" \
        "gtimeout" "${_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[0]}"
else
    assert_fail "[#1752/SPEC-1] _ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[0] is gtimeout on gtimeout-only PATH" \
        "_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT is empty — no timeout binary found on gtimeout-only PATH"
fi

# ── [#1752/SPEC-2]: no timeout binary leaves _ACCEPTANCE_TOUT empty ──────────
print_test_section "[#1752/SPEC-2] no timeout binary leaves _ACCEPTANCE_TOUT empty, returns 0"

_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT=()
unset _ACCEPTANCE_TIMEOUT_KILL_OK
export PATH="/nonexistent-path-$$"
_spec2_rc=0
_acceptance_timeout_prefix 30 || _spec2_rc=$?
export PATH="$_SAVED_PATH"

assert_eq "[#1752/SPEC-2] returns 0 when no timeout binary" "0" "$_spec2_rc"
assert_eq "[#1752/SPEC-2] _ACCEPTANCE_TOUT is empty when no timeout binary" \
    "0" "${#_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[@]}"

# ── [#1752/SPEC-3]: build false-completion guard still detects inert_build ────
print_test_section "[#1752/SPEC-3] build false-completion guard detects red testfile after helper is shared"

# Minimal mocks so plugin.sh sources without LLM calls or event-bus writes.
# shellcheck disable=SC2317
route_to_model_loop() {
    _ROUTE_LOOP_ITERATIONS=1
    _ROUTE_LOOP_TERMINATED_REASON="done_sentinel"
    _ROUTE_LOOP_INPUT_TOKENS=0
    _ROUTE_LOOP_OUTPUT_TOKENS=0
    _ROUTE_LOOP_LAST_RESPONSE="LOOP_COMPLETE"
    return 0
}
# shellcheck disable=SC2317
_route_resolve_max_iterations() { echo 3; }
# shellcheck disable=SC2317
_route_loop_close_final_banner() { return 0; }
# shellcheck disable=SC2317
apply_scope_redaction() {
    local _in="$1" _out="$2"
    [[ -f "$_in" ]] && cp "$_in" "$_out"
    return 0
}

export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/artifacts"

# shellcheck source=../../plugins/agent/build/plugin.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/agent/build/plugin.sh"

_S3_REPO="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s3-repo"
mkdir -p "$_S3_REPO"
(
    cd "$_S3_REPO"
    git init -q
    git config user.email t@t
    git config user.name t
    printf 'seed\n' > seed.txt
    git add seed.txt
    git commit -q -m seed
) >/dev/null

mkdir -p "$_S3_REPO/tests/unit"
cat > "$_S3_REPO/tests/unit/always-fail-test.sh" <<'FAIL_EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
exit 1
FAIL_EOF
chmod +x "$_S3_REPO/tests/unit/always-fail-test.sh"

# Reset timeout memo so the guard's _acceptance_timeout_prefix re-probes cleanly.
_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT=()
unset _ACCEPTANCE_TIMEOUT_KILL_OK

_s3_failing=""
_s3_rc=0
_s3_failing="$(_build_guard_false_completion \
    "tests/unit/always-fail-test.sh" "$_S3_REPO" 2>/dev/null)" || _s3_rc=$?

assert_eq "[#1752/SPEC-3] guard exits 1 for red testfile (signals inert_build to caller)" \
    "1" "$_s3_rc"
assert_eq "[#1752/SPEC-3] guard returns the failing testfile path" \
    "tests/unit/always-fail-test.sh" "$_s3_failing"

# ── [#1752/SPEC-9]: five non-acceptance-gate sites produce gtimeout ────────────
print_test_section "[#1752/SPEC-9] each converted site produces gtimeout on gtimeout-only host"

_s9_labels=(
    "core/router/route.sh sync path"
    "core/router/route.sh loop path"
    "scripts/run-tests.sh"
    "scripts/run-mutation.sh"
    "scripts/lib/gh-automation.sh"
)
for _s9_label in "${_s9_labels[@]}"; do
    _ACCEPTANCE_TOUT=()
    unset _ACCEPTANCE_TIMEOUT_KILL_OK
    export PATH="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/fakebin"
    _acceptance_timeout_prefix 60
    export PATH="$_SAVED_PATH"
    if [[ "${#_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[@]}" -gt 0 ]]; then
        assert_eq "[#1752/SPEC-9] $_s9_label: _ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[0]=gtimeout" \
            "gtimeout" "${_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[0]}"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1752/SPEC-9] $_s9_label: _ACCEPTANCE_TOUT non-empty" \
            "_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT is empty — gtimeout not found on gtimeout-only PATH"
    fi
done

# ── [#1752/SPEC-10]: per-caller kill-grace env bridge ─────────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1752/SPEC-10] per-caller kill-grace env bridge"

# run-tests.sh bridge: ZBUILD_TEST_KILL_GRACE=42
ZBUILD_TEST_KILL_GRACE=42
_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT=()
unset _ACCEPTANCE_TIMEOUT_KILL_OK
export PATH="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/fakebin"
export ZBUILD_NEGCTL_KILL_GRACE="${ZBUILD_TEST_KILL_GRACE:-10}"
_acceptance_timeout_prefix 60
export PATH="$_SAVED_PATH"

# With -k supported: _ACCEPTANCE_TOUT = [gtimeout, -k, <grace>, <timeout_s>]
if [[ "${#_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[@]}" -ge 4 ]]; then
    assert_eq "[#1752/SPEC-10] run-tests.sh bridge: kill grace index 2 is 42" \
        "42" "${_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[2]}"
    assert_eq "[#1752/SPEC-10] run-tests.sh bridge: element 1 is -k flag" \
        "-k" "${_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[1]}"
else
    assert_fail "[#1752/SPEC-10] run-tests.sh bridge: _ACCEPTANCE_TOUT has -k and grace" \
        "array too short (${#_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[@]} elements): ${_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[*]:-empty}"
fi

# run-mutation.sh bridge: ZBUILD_MUTATION_KILL_GRACE=7
ZBUILD_MUTATION_KILL_GRACE=7
_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT=()
unset _ACCEPTANCE_TIMEOUT_KILL_OK
export PATH="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/fakebin"
export ZBUILD_NEGCTL_KILL_GRACE="${ZBUILD_MUTATION_KILL_GRACE:-10}"
_acceptance_timeout_prefix 300
export PATH="$_SAVED_PATH"

if [[ "${#_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[@]}" -ge 4 ]]; then
    assert_eq "[#1752/SPEC-10] run-mutation.sh bridge: kill grace index 2 is 7" \
        "7" "${_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[2]}"
    assert_eq "[#1752/SPEC-10] run-mutation.sh bridge: element 1 is -k flag" \
        "-k" "${_ACCEPTANCE_TOUT[1]}"
else
    assert_fail "[#1752/SPEC-10] run-mutation.sh bridge: _ACCEPTANCE_TOUT has -k and grace" \

fi

# Tests: scripts/lib/lint-bare-timeout.sh (#1752)

#   SPEC-5: scripts/release.sh line ~629 carries a lint-bare-timeout:allow comment
#   SPEC-6: ADR-036 amendment names _acceptance_timeout_prefix, timeout-cmd.sh, Enforced-by

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

print_test_header "lint-bare-timeout.sh — bare timeout detection and exemption (#1752)"
setup_test_env "lint-bare-timeout"
_test_cleanup_hook() { cleanup_test_env; }

LINT="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/lint-bare-timeout.sh"
T="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/tree"
mkdir -p "$T"

_run_lint() {
    local _dir="${1:-$T}"
    local _rc=0
    bash "$LINT" "$_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1 || _rc=$?
    printf '%s' "$_rc"
}

# ── [#1752/SPEC-4]: linter behavior on fixtures ───────────────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1752/SPEC-4] linter exits 1 on bare timeout; exits 0 on clean fixture"

_pkg="$REPO_ROOT/package.json"
_lint_script=""

if grep -qF "lint-bare-timeout.sh" <<< "$_lint_script" 2>/dev/null; then

_live_rc=0

_live_out="$(bash "$LINT" 2>&1)" || _live_rc=$?
assert_eq "[#1752/SPEC-7] running lint-bare-timeout.sh on the repo tree exits 0" \
    "0" "$_live_rc"
if [[ "$_live_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$_live_out" >&2
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results

    local timeout_s="$1"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Per-tier test runner. Usage: scripts/run-tests.sh --tier {unit,integration,e2e,golden,mutation,lint,all}
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
TESTS_DIR="${ZBUILD_TESTS_DIR:-$REPO_ROOT/tests}"
PLUGINS_DIR="${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_DIR:-$REPO_ROOT/plugins}"
CORE_DIR="${ZBUILD_CORE_DIR:-$REPO_ROOT/core}"

# #929: per-file isolation so a non-test or hanging file can never wedge the run
# (a markdown mutation spec executed as bash blocked on stdin for 3.5h in a
# #911 dogfood). Bounds EACH individual test-file invocation in both the
# --files and tier loops — NOT the mutation orchestrator, which is a separate
# long-running invocation. Override the bound via ZBUILD_TEST_FILE_TIMEOUT
# (seconds; 0 disables). Degrades to no-timeout when neither gtimeout nor
# timeout is installed (best-effort, same convention as core/router/route.sh).
# #1157: default 300→480. The spawn-heavy core-pipeline-runner suite (un-gated
# onto macOS) legitimately needs ~300s on the slow shared macOS runner, leaving
# no headroom for runner-speed variance. 480 gives margin without masking a real
# hang (a genuinely wedged file still fails, just later). Overridable as before.
_RT_FILE_TIMEOUT="${ZBUILD_TEST_FILE_TIMEOUT:-480}"
# #1660: plain `timeout` sends TERM only, so a file that traps or ignores TERM
# outruns its bound entirely. `-k` escalates to KILL after a grace period
# (ZBUILD_TEST_KILL_GRACE, default 10s), making the bound real; worst-case
# per-file wall-clock becomes _RT_FILE_TIMEOUT + the grace. The flag is probed,
# not assumed — a `timeout` that lacks it would exit 125 on every single file
# rather than running it, so an unsupporting binary degrades to the TERM-only
# bound instead of failing the suite.
_RT_KILL_GRACE="${ZBUILD_TEST_KILL_GRACE:-10}"
_rt_tout=()
if [[ "$_RT_FILE_TIMEOUT" != "0" ]]; then
  _rt_tout_bin=""
  if   command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then _rt_tout_bin="gtimeout"
  elif command -v timeout  >/dev/null 2>&1; then _rt_tout_bin="timeout"
  fi
  if [[ -n "$_rt_tout_bin" ]]; then
    if "$_rt_tout_bin" -k 1 1 true >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      _rt_tout=("$_rt_tout_bin" "-k" "$_RT_KILL_GRACE" "$_RT_FILE_TIMEOUT")
    else
      _rt_tout=("$_rt_tout_bin" "$_RT_FILE_TIMEOUT")
    fi
  fi
fi

# _rt_is_timeout_rc <rc> — true when the rc is the shape a killed file exits
# with (#1613). 124 = GNU timeout/gtimeout gave up; 137 = SIGKILL (128+9);
# 143 = SIGTERM (128+15), which is what the file sees when `timeout` signals it.
# A test that deliberately exits one of these is indistinguishable — accepted:
# the bound is the far likelier cause, and mislabelling a hang as an assertion
# failure is the failure mode this exists to stop.
_rt_is_timeout_rc() {
  case "${1:-}" in 124|137|143) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
}

# Sole renderer of a summary note; concatenated, not IFS-joined (that join uses only IFS's first char and drops the space).
_rt_build_note() {
    local _sk="${1:-0}" _to="${2:-0}" _note=""
    [[ "${_sk:-0}" -gt 0 ]] && _note="$_sk skipped"
    [[ "${_to:-0}" -gt 0 ]] && _note="${_note:+$_note, }$_to timed out"
    [[ -n "$_note" ]] && printf ' (%s)' "$_note"
    return 0
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/router/route.sh — ADR-003 model router stub (issue #84)
# Maps tier ordinals (T0-T4) to concrete models via config/models.json.
# Phase 0.5: picks candidates[0]; UCB1 bandit deferred to #29.
# Sourced by callers — no set -euo pipefail at file scope (would mutate caller options).

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ROUTER_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_ROUTER_LOADED=1

_ROUTER_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
_ZBUILD_ROOT="$(cd "$_ROUTER_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
# Opens the read-only scope block for a stage that may not change the
# repository; also its idempotence guard (_route_redact_prompt).
_ZB_READ_ONLY_SCOPE_MARKER='## YOUR SCOPE (engine-provided)'

# ─── _route_has_done_sentinel <sentinel> <text> ─────────────────────────────
# rc 0 when some LINE of <text> is the sentinel once whitespace and punctuation
# are removed and case is ignored: `LOOP_COMPLETE.`, `**LOOP_COMPLETE**`,
# `Loop complete!` all count; a sentence that merely MENTIONS it does not.
# #1847 run 20260928102849-23575: design wrote "LOOP_COMPLETE." in 8 of 14
# answers, the exact-line match missed every one, and each miss bought another
# full model call (10 calls, ~41 min, for one design iteration).
_route_has_done_sentinel() {
    awk -v s="${1:-}" '
        BEGIN { s = toupper(s); gsub(/[^A-Z0-9]/, "", s); if (s == "") exit 1 }
        { l = toupper($0); gsub(/[^A-Z0-9]/, "", l); if (l == s) { found = 1; exit } }
        # END runs even after an `exit` above; `found` is unset (0) unless a
        # line matched, so an empty sentinel or no match both exit 1.
        END { exit(found ? 0 : 1) }' <<< "${2:-}"
}

# ─── base-include guard (#1624) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# route.sh is the base include for EVERY routing plugin, so one bad library here
# takes down all dispatch at once. One helper rather than nine inline copies, so
# the policy cannot drift between call sites.
#
# `exit`, not `return`: no caller checks `source route.sh`'s status (verified —
# all 8+ call sites are a bare `source`), so returning would let a plugin run on
# with the router half-loaded, which is the silent failure this issue exists to
# remove.
#
# Syntax is checked with `bash -n` rather than `source X || …`: source returns
# the LAST command's status, so a well-formed library ending in a merely-falsy
# statement would be misreported as broken. `bash -n` parses without executing.
#
# bash's own parse error carries the line and token; it is captured and FORWARDED
# rather than discarded. Sending it to /dev/null would name the broken file while
# deleting the only text saying what is broken about it — strictly worse for the
# operator than the unguarded original, on an issue whose whole point is
# diagnosability (PR #1651 review; the pattern #1631 exists to lint for).

local _register_interval="${ZBUILD_SHIP_CHECKS_REGISTER_INTERVAL:-5}"
    local _waited=0 _probe
    while :; do
        _probe="$("$gh_pr_cmd" pr checks "$pr_ref" --required 2>&1 || true)"
        grep -q 'no checks reported' <<< "$_probe" || break
        (( _waited >= _register_grace )) && break
        sleep "$_register_interval"
        _waited=$(( _waited + _register_interval ))
    done
    if ! timeout "$checks_timeout" "$gh_pr_cmd" pr checks "$pr_ref" --watch --fail-fast --required; then
        error "release --ship: PR #${pr_ref} required checks failed or timed out (${checks_timeout}s) — NOT merging or publishing (PR left open)"
        exit 1
    fi
    success "release --ship: [4/7] PR #${pr_ref} checks passed"

    # ── Step 5/7: confirm gate (skipped when --yes / ZBUILD_SHIP_YES=1) ───────
    # Prompt goes to stderr so it appears even when stdout is piped.
    # ZBUILD_SHIP_CONFIRM_ANSWER seam: when set, its value IS the answer (a plain
    # string, never executed) — allows non-interactive tests without a real TTY.
    info "release --ship: [5/7] confirm: version ${version}, tag ${tag}, PR #${pr_ref}"

1	# ADR-036 — Acceptance-contract teeth (mechanical SPEC↔assertion gate)
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted (2026-06-17); amended 2026-07-01 (role/strategy split + preconditions);
4	amended 2026-07-03 (#1218, ADR-046 — Level-1 SPEC-tag-presence shifts LEFT to a PRE-build
5	`design-gate`; this post-build acceptance-gate retains Level-2 negative-control/tautology +
6	Level-3 reachability, which cannot shift left — they need a built assertion + baseline-vs-HEAD)
7	**Related:** ADR-031 (behavioral acceptance contract), ADR-013 (canonical stage list),
8	ADR-020 (inter-stage data contract / optional inputs), ADR-022 (test-assessment),
9	ADR-030 (scope governance), ADR-042 (plug-and-play stage resolution),
10	ADR-046 (design-verify shift-left)
11	**Issue:** #922 (843-F). Surfaced by the dogfood of #844.
12	
13	## Amendment (2026-07-01) — generic role, method-named plugin, declarative preconditions
14	
15	The gate is split into a **generic slot** and a **named strategy**:
16	
17	- **Role `acceptance_gate`** — the generic slot: "verify a design's acceptance
18	  contract." Template stage id stays `acceptance-gate` (an ADR-013 canonical
19	  leaf, unchanged); it binds `roles: [acceptance_gate]`.
20	- **Plugin `spec-acceptance`** — the method: the SPEC-block negative-control +
21	  wiring-reachability strategy described below. The plugin dir/manifest id was
22	  renamed `acceptance-gate → spec-acceptance` (method-named). Role-then-id
23	  resolution (ADR-042) dispatches the stage to it, so a different repo may bind
24	  a *different* plugin to `acceptance_gate` without adopting SPEC. The result
25	  artifact keeps its slot-scoped name `acceptance-gate-result.json` (readers
26	  resolve it via `provides.artifact_type`, not a literal).
27	- **Declarative `preconditions`** (manifest, machine-readable) generalize the
28	  old "no-op when the acceptance block is absent" (§4). When any precondition is
29	  unmet the gate no-ops (`verdict=pass`, `reason=precondition_unmet`,
30	  `precondition=<id>`): (1) `design_acceptance_block` present, (2)
31	  `merge_base_resolvable`, (3) `tagged_testfiles` — the block declares a
32	  contract to check. These gate **applicability**, not correctness: a
33	  declared-but-missing TESTFILE or a malformed block is still a genuine
34	  violation (teeth preserved), not a no-op.
35	
36	## Context
37	
38	ADR-031 introduced the behavioral acceptance contract: `design` emits an
39	```` ```acceptance ```` block of `SPEC:` lines + `TESTFILES:`, writes failing
40	stubs, `build` makes them pass, and `test_assessment` judges whether each SPEC
41	holds. But ADR-031 explicitly left the teeth as **convention, not tooling**
42	("*Design writes failing tests … enforced by convention, not by tooling*";
43	"*Don't-weaken charter … enforced by process, not automation*").
44	
45	The hole: nothing links an individual SPEC to an assertion that would **fail
46	without the implementation**. A SPEC passes if its TESTFILES are merely green
47	and the (LLM) `test_assessment` believes the prose — it "passes on LLM grounding
48	alone."
49	
50	**Live proof — #844.** The regression test
51	`tests/unit/cycle-g2-cross-iter-timeout-test.sh` went green **even with the
52	implementation's seeding loop deleted** (its abandon assertions used
53	`MOCK_PLAN="build:timeout"`, hitting the within-run threshold regardless of the
54	feature). `test_assessment` returned `pass`; the headline behavior was never
55	actually exercised. A tautological test the contract could not detect.
56	
57	## Decision
58	
59	Add a mechanical, **non-LLM** `acceptance-gate` stage (a canonical leaf stage,
60	ADR-013 amendment) that gives the contract teeth in two levels.
61	
62	### 1. Stable SPEC ids + assertion tagging
63	
64	`SPEC:` lines gain stable ids: `SPEC-1:`, `SPEC-2:`, … (permanent across
65	iterations). Each backing assertion must carry its id in the assert **label**,
66	e.g. `assert_eq "[SPEC-2] carry-over count" exp act`. (`acceptance-block.sh`
67	keeps parsing legacy bare `SPEC:` lines for back-compat; only `SPEC-n:` lines
68	carry an id the gate enforces.)
69	
70	### 2. Level 1 — tag-presence (cheap, fail-fast)
71	
72	`acceptance-coverage.sh`: every `SPEC-n` must have ≥1 `[SPEC-n]`-tagged
73	assertion across the declared TESTFILES. A SPEC with none fails the gate
74	(`acceptance.gate.untagged_spec`).
75	
76	### 3. Level 2 — baseline negative control (the real teeth)
77	
78	`acceptance-negctl.sh`: each `SPEC-n`'s tagged TESTFILE must **fail at the
79	merge-base baseline and pass at HEAD**. Mechanism: a detached `git worktree` at
80	the merge-base with the default branch (resolved by the shared
81	`scripts/lib/merge-base.sh`, the same basis review uses, #896), with the TESTFILE
82	overlaid from HEAD (implementation reverted, test current). A valid control ⇔
83	`rc_baseline != 0 AND rc_head == 0`. A SPEC whose tagged test passes at baseline
84	is **tautological** and is rejected (`acceptance.gate.tautology`); a stub that
85	never passes is rejected (`not_passing_at_head`). Granularity is per-TESTFILE;
86	author one SPEC per assertion for precise attribution.
87	
88	When the merge-base equals HEAD (no implementation delta) the control is
89	skipped, not failed (`NEGCTL SKIP <spec_id> no_impl_delta`, one line per declared
90	SPEC — see the #1715 amendment).
91	
92	### 4. Composability — declarative preconditions, no-op when unmet
93	
94	The gate declares the design/acceptance artifact as an **optional input**
95	(`required: false`, ADR-020 convention) and a machine-readable `preconditions`
96	block (see the 2026-07-01 amendment). When any precondition is unmet — no
97	acceptance block, unresolvable merge-base, or a placeholder block with nothing
98	to check — it is a **no-op pass** (`acceptance.gate.skipped`,
99	`reason=precondition_unmet`), so it drops cleanly into any template (including
100	repos that do not use SPEC) and is omittable from any other — honoring stage
101	independence.
102	
103	### 5. Placement
104	
105	In the standard template the gate runs inside `build_review_cycle` immediately after
106	`build_test_cycle`, before the CQ stages — a broken acceptance contract fails
107	fast. Because it is its own stage it does **not** depend on `test_assessment`
108	changes (#867).
109	
110	## Consequences
111	
112	- The #844 defect class (green-but-inert tautological tests) is now caught
113	  mechanically, not left to LLM judgment.
114	- `design`/`build` prompts are updated to emit `SPEC-n:` ids and `[SPEC-n]`
115	  tags. Anti-patterns (tautological tag, logic-in-helper, multi-SPEC-per-label,
116	  unconditional mocks) are stated in the prompts.
117	- ADR-031's "convention / process" clauses for test-first enforcement and the
118	  don't-weaken charter are **superseded** by this mechanical gate.
119	- New events registered in `config/event-schema.json`:
120	  `acceptance.gate.{start,complete,skipped,untagged_spec,tautology,baseline_resolve_failed,worktree_failed}`.
121	- ADR-013 grows by one canonical leaf stage (`acceptance-gate`), 16 → 17.
122	
123	## Implementation Notes
124	
125	- **Libraries** (`scripts/lib/`): `acceptance-coverage.sh` (Level 1 tag-presence),
126	  `acceptance-negctl.sh` (Level 2 negative control), and `merge-base.sh`
127	  (`zbuild_resolve_merge_base`, extracted from review's private resolver so the
128	  gate does not source the review plugin). SPEC-id parsing + `acceptance_list_spec_ids`
129	  / `acceptance_list_testfiles` live in the existing `acceptance-block.sh`.
130	- **Negative-control mechanism**: a detached `git worktree add --detach <merge-base>`
131	  with each declared TESTFILE overlaid via `git show HEAD:<path>`; the test runs
132	  with `ZBUILD_TEST_QUIET` unset and a hard timeout (`ZBUILD_NEGCTL_TIMEOUT`,
133	  default 60s). The validity test is rc-based at the file level: `rc_baseline != 0
134	  && rc_head == 0`. The worktree is removed via a `RETURN` trap.
135	- **Plugin** (`plugins/agent/spec-acceptance/`, role `acceptance_gate`; renamed
136	  from `acceptance-gate` per the 2026-07-01 amendment): `kind: agent`, modeled on
137	  `cq-preflight`; writes `acceptance-gate-result.json` (`{"verdict","failures"}`),
138	  returns rc=1 on fail (picked up mechanically by `runner_read_stage_verdict`'s
139	  `*` branch — no `verdict.sh` change). `design` is declared `required: false`.
140	- **Wiring**: `build_review_cycle.flow` (after `build_test_cycle`), `_ZBUILD_CANONICAL_STAGES`
141	  (template.sh, 16→17), `_LC_STAGE_IDS_TO_CHECK` (lint-contract.sh), the test roster
142	  (`_ZBUILD_STANDARD_ROSTER` + `register_standard_pipeline_stubs`, #921), ADR-013,
143	  and the event schema.
144	- **Adding a stage cost (ABS-1)**: this change touched ~14 roster/position/count
145	  test sites despite #921's single-source helper, because the remaining sites are
146	  intentional tripwires and custom-body tests. Future stage additions should reuse
147	  `register_standard_pipeline_stubs` wherever a test only needs a pass-through roster.
148	
149	## Limitations / future work
150	
151	- Per-TESTFILE granularity: a file mixing a load-bearing and a tautological SPEC
152	  is judged load-bearing. The prompt mandates one SPEC per assertion to mitigate.
153	- The review-side coverage complement (downgrade `approve` when a SPEC's test is
154	  untouched in the diff) is tracked separately (843-H / #923).
155	
156	## Amendment (#951, 2026-06-18) — closing the coverage-gap loop to build
157	
158	The gate runs as a `build_review_cycle` member after `build_test_cycle` and before
159	`review`, writing `acceptance-gate-result.json` (`failures[]`) and coercing review's
160	verdict on a coverage gap. But that finding reached build only one outer iteration

182	## Amendment (#956, 2026-06-19) — Level 3: reachability (the wiring negative control)
183	
184	Level 2 reverts the *implementation* and requires a SPEC test to fail — proving the
185	code does real work. It cannot prove the code is *reached by the production path*: a
186	new library implemented but never wired into the live dispatch still passes, because
187	the SPEC test exercises it directly. This is the "green but inert" class (#845 plateau
188	detector never wired into `standard.yaml`; #913 live-flow post-condition gated on a
189	token authors never emitted).

191	Level 3 is the **dual of the Level-2 negative control** — an integration-level ablation
192	that reverts the *wiring* instead of the implementation:
193	
194	- **`WIRING:` declaration** in the ```acceptance block names the separable file(s) that
195	  activate the behavior in the live path (a `config/templates/*.yaml` flow entry, a
196	  dispatch/registration file), one repo-relative path per line. `WIRING: none` is an
197	  explicit pure-utility exemption (recorded via `acceptance.gate.wiring_exempt`, never a
198	  silent skip). Parsed by `acceptance_list_wiring` (`scripts/lib/acceptance-block.sh`);
199	  absolute / `..` paths are rejected by the path-traversal guard.
200	- **`acceptance-reachability.sh`** creates a detached worktree at the merge-base, overlays
201	  every changed file from HEAD EXCEPT the WIRING target (leaving the wiring at baseline),
202	  re-runs the declared TESTFILES, and requires ≥1 to flip pass→fail. No flip →
203	  `REACHABILITY FAIL inert_wiring <target>`.
204	  **Amended 2026-09-16 (#2109):** the flip is judged per `[SPEC-n]` line (the #1969 rule
205	  negctl applies), file rc only where the captures carry no verdict — and "no flip" is
206	  no longer one word. A TESTFILE red at HEAD is
207	  `REACHABILITY FAIL not_passing_at_head <target> <tf>` (build's defect, the same class
208	  negctl reports per SPEC; recoverable, escalates on iter≥2 per #2097); a run the harness
209	  could not execute (rc 126/127) is `REACHABILITY ERROR harness:<target> <tf>` (advisory,
210	  never a flip or a violation); a roster with no declared TESTFILE on disk is
211	  `REACHABILITY FAIL no_testfiles <target>` (recoverable). `inert_wiring` is reserved for
212	  the case it names: every TESTFILE green at HEAD and none flips. On #1841 the old label
213	  sent a plain build defect (an unimplemented SPEC) to design as `fault: specification`.

216	  — and every SPEC bound to it is judged from those captures; the per-SPEC
217	  `negctl-<spec>.log` sections are replayed from the memo. It used to run the whole file
218	  twice PER SPEC: 18 SPECs on one 129s file = 38 executions, 68 minutes per pass (#1840).
219	  The per-run bound is `max(negctl_timeout_s, 3× the file's time as MEASURED by the test

226	  `acceptance.gate.inert_wiring` emitted), coercing review like every other gate failure.

247	## Amendment (#1188, 2026-07-01) — timeout classification + infra failures are non-terminal
248	
249	The gate is mechanical, so a false hard-fail halts the whole pipeline (rc=8) **(superseded 2026-10-08 by ADR-054 §4 / #1850 — now rc 1 + `_CYCLE_LAST_OUTCOME=failed`)** with no
250	recovery. Two robustness gaps caused exactly that:
251	
252	1. **Timeout misclassification.** Each SPEC test runs under `timeout ${ZBUILD_NEGCTL_TIMEOUT}`
253	   (rc 124, or 143 when the child dies from the SIGTERM). A timeout leaves the test's true
254	   pass/fail *unknown*, yet the old rc-based logic folded a HEAD-run timeout into the genuine
255	   `not_passing_at_head` class, and a BASELINE-run timeout spuriously satisfied the valid
256	   control (`rc_base != 0 && rc_head == 0`) → a **false PASS**. Fix: `_negctl_run` /
257	   `_reachability_run` detect rc 124/143; a timeout on EITHER run is an INFRA signal that is
258	   never a control, a violation, or a wiring flip. It emits a distinct class
259	   `negctl_error:timeout:<sid>` (reachability: `reachability_error:timeout:<target>`) with a
260	   dedicated `acceptance.gate.negctl_timeout` / `acceptance.gate.reachability_timeout` event.
261	
262	2. **Infra failures were terminal.** `_cycle_acceptance_terminal_failure` (cycle-orchestrator)
263	   treated every failure class except `untagged_spec:` as terminal. Now the INFRA classes
264	   `negctl_error:*` and `reachability_error:*` (resolve/worktree failures AND the new timeout
265	   class) are ALSO non-terminal — a flaky/slow sandbox must not hard-fail the pipeline as if
266	   the contract were violated. GENUINE violations stay terminal: `tautology`,
267	   `not_passing_at_head`, `inert_wiring`, `no_testfile`, `malformed_acceptance_block`.
268	
269	**Configurable timeout + captured output.** `ZBUILD_NEGCTL_TIMEOUT` is an overridable per-stage
270	knob: templates declare `negctl_timeout_s:` on the `acceptance-gate` stage (read lazily via
271	`template_stage_negctl_timeout` from the loaded template source — no row-shape change); the
272	plugin resolves precedence **env `ZBUILD_NEGCTL_TIMEOUT` > per-stage template > 60s default**
273	(env wins so CI/operators can force a value) and exports it plus `ZBUILD_NEGCTL_ARTIFACT_DIR`
274	to the libs. Each SPEC / WIRING run now appends its combined output to a size-bounded
275	(`64 KiB`) `artifacts/negctl-<sid>.log` / `artifacts/reachability-<target>.log` so a failed
276	control is diagnosable instead of silently `>/dev/null`.

279	
280	The #1188 amendment above still described the **engine** classifying the gate's failure
281	vocabulary (`_cycle_acceptance_terminal_failure` knew the literal class strings). That coupling
282	is now removed: the plugin OWNS the class→disposition mapping and writes a generic
283	`disposition` field into `acceptance-gate-result.json`; the cycle engine reads only that field
284	(see ADR-021, generic member-disposition contract). Mapping (`_ag_classify_disposition`,
285	precedence highest-first):
286	
287	| disposition   | failure classes                                                            | engine effect                                             |
288	| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |

298	## Amendment (#1211, 2026-07-03) — nested-test stage-io isolated + concise operator summary
299	
300	The Level-2 negctl and Level-3 reachability checks shell out `bash <TESTFILE>` (`_negctl_run`,
301	`_reachability_run`). The runner dups fd 3 to the operator terminal and exports
302	`ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_FD=3` so stage-io banners survive `2>/dev/null` (`core/pipeline/runner.sh`, the
303	fd-3 contract). Those two sandbox runners redirected only fd 1+2 into the diagnostic logfile,
304	leaving **fd 3 and `ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_FD=3` inherited untouched** — so a nested TESTFILE that drives
305	real plugins (review / security-lens / test_assessment mocks) had their stage-io banners escape
306	straight to the operator terminal, bypassing the sandbox capture and repeating once per
307	baseline/HEAD run × SPEC/WIRING target. Observed in the #944 dogfood (run 20260703154556): dozens
308	of raw `# Review … Verdict:` fixtures, full security-lens prompts, and `_empty lens result_` lines
309	flooding the terminal.
310	
311	Fix (two parts, both repo-agnostic — fd handling + verdict strings carry no plugin/language/path
312	assumptions):
313	
314	1. **Close the fd-3 escape.** Both sandbox runners now `unset ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_FD` (nested banners
315	   fall back to fd 2, already captured by `2>&1`) and redirect/close fd 3 (`3>>"$logfile"` when a
316	   diagnostic log is configured, else `3>&-`). Nested output is captured into the diagnostic log,
317	   never the terminal.
318	2. **Concise operator summary.** The plugin surfaces the already-computed structured verdict lines
319	   (`NEGCTL PASS/FAIL <spec>`, `REACHABILITY PASS/FAIL <target>`) as ONE line per SPEC and per
320	   WIRING target via the acceptance-gate stage's own `[file,stdout]` stage-io (`_ag_emit_operator_summary`,
321	   io-gated on the stage's destinations, routed to `ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_FD`). Reuses the ADR-039
322	   file-only-child + prose-summary pattern (the review lenses do the same).
323	
324	This is the stage-io instance of the general nested-isolation gap tracked in **#1127** (ANY nested
325	pipeline/test execution isolating its stage-io fd from the parent). The durable, engine-wide fix is
326	deferred there; #1211 closes only the two acceptance-gate sandbox runners.

328	## Amendment (#1219, 2026-07-04) — tautology is DESIGN-ROOTED → routes back to design
329	
330	> **Superseded by Amendment #1583 (below).** #1219 routed a tautology back to design on the
331	> premise that design authors the assertion. #1477 (commit 8f89dd1) removed design's stub-writer,
332	> making **build** the author of all assertion bodies — so routing tautology to design became a
333	> dead end (design can only edit `design.md` declarations, which are already correct). #1583 makes
334	> tautology **build-fixable** instead. The text below is retained for history.
335	
336	The Level-2 negative control classifies a `[change]` SPEC whose tagged assertion PASSES at the
337	merge-base baseline as **tautological** (`tautology:<spec>`): the test asserts nothing, the classic
338	"green but inert" defect. The build stage is **forbidden** to fix this — ADR-036's whole point is
339	that build must not touch acceptance assertions (else it games the gate). The only correct fix is to
340	**re-author the SPEC**, which is the province of the stage that authored it: **design**.
341	
342	Therefore, on a tautology failure, the acceptance-gate adds a generic scalar `route_target: "design"`
343	to `acceptance-gate-result.json` (verdict / disposition / rc UNCHANGED — still `fail` / `terminal` /
344	rc=1, which yields the `member_terminal_failure` rc=8 **(superseded 2026-10-08 by ADR-054 §4 / #1850 — now rc 1 + `_CYCLE_LAST_OUTCOME=failed`)** the route_back guard needs). The
345	gate-aggregator rolls a failed gate's `route_target` up into `verdict == route_design`, and
346	`simple.yaml`'s `build_test_cycle` route_back (ADR-045) rewinds to `design_verify_cycle` (ADR-046)
347	so design re-authors the assertion, reading the focused `design-feedback.md` the aggregator wrote.
348	
349	**Design-rooted vs build-fixable.** ONLY `tautology` is design-rooted. The other classes set NO
350	`route_target` on the first attempt: `not_passing_at_head` (fix the impl or the assertion —
351	recoverable since Amendment #2097), `no_testfile` / `untagged_spec` (add the tagged assertion —
352	recoverable, fed to build via the #951 edge), `inert_wiring` (make the WIRING load-bearing),
353	`malformed_acceptance_block` (terminal). The plugin-vocabulary → generic-field (`route_target`)
354	mapping lives ENTIRELY in the acceptance-gate plugin (ADR-021: the engine and the aggregator know
355	no acceptance-gate failure vocabulary).

357	## Amendment (#1265, 2026-07-06) — `no_impl_delta` SKIP is legit ONLY as a clean `empty_diff` resting point
358	
359	The acceptance-gate negative-control + reachability checks `SKIP` with `no_impl_delta` when there is no committed diff to judge (`base_sha == head_sha`, 0 commits ahead). That SKIP is correct for a genuine **nothing-to-do** convergence — a build that reached `LOOP_COMPLETE` with an empty diff and green gates (`verdict=empty_diff`, `#1208`/`#895`). It is a **false pass** when the branch is empty for the WRONG reason: a `scope_violation` discarded the whole diff (`#1214` dogfood), so `npm test` passed on the *uncommitted* tree, the gate SKIPped, the gate-aggregator passed, and the cycle **converged on nothing** — sailing to a confusing `pr`-stage abort (`No commits between main and branch`) ~38 min later.
360	
361	- **0-commit + build verdict ≠ `empty_diff` is NOT a resting point.** The cycle orchestrator adds a `no_committed_changes` guard (see ADR-021 amendment): a convergence that would fire with 0 commits ahead of the intake baseline AND `build.verdict != empty_diff` is suppressed and terminated (`no_committed_changes`, rc=5, blocked-class → halts before review/`pr`), unless a governed scope grant is pending (`#870`/`#840` — the next iter commits).
362	- **The `empty_diff` resting point is EXEMPT.** A true clean `empty_diff` converge with 0 real commits genuinely has nothing to ship; the `no_impl_delta` SKIP and convergence both remain correct. No `#1208`/`#895` regression.
363	- **`pr`-stage backstop.** `pr-open` resolves the merge-base and refuses (`plugin.run.error reason=no_committed_changes`, rc=2) BEFORE push + `gh pr create` when 0 commits ahead — belt-and-suspenders for non-cycle paths and the confusing `gh` error.

366	## Amendment (#1583, 2026-07-23) — tautology is BUILD-FIXABLE → routes to build with enriched diagnosis
367	
368	**Supersedes the routing decision of Amendment #1219.** #1219 routed a `tautology` failure back to
369	**design** on the premise that design authored the assertion and build was forbidden to touch it.
370	That premise no longer holds: **#1477 (commit 8f89dd1) removed design's stub-writer**, so the
371	**build** stage now authors every test assertion body, and `design.md` carries only the acceptance
372	*declarations* (SPEC ids + TESTFILES bindings). Routing a tautology to design became a **deadlock** —
373	design can only re-emit its (already-correct) declarations, build is forbidden to touch the
374	assertion, so neither stage can fix it and the `build_test_cycle` route-back budget exhausts to
375	`rc=8`. Live evidence: issue #1576 failed this way three times (~8h) with a byte-identical
376	re-authored acceptance block each pass.
377	
378	Decision: **a tautology is build-fixable.** Re-authoring a *false* assertion into a genuine one is
379	orthogonal to the don't-weaken charter (which forbids relaxing a *real* requirement). Concretely:
380	
381	- The acceptance-gate **no longer sets `route_target: "design"`** for a tautology
382	  (`plugins/agent/spec-acceptance/plugin.sh`). Tautology stays a terminal failure but flows through
383	  the existing `gate_feedback -> build` edge and re-iterates inside `build_test_cycle`.
384	- **Build is told, precisely, what to fix.** Build reads the flagged `tautology:<id>` ids
385	  (`_build_read_tautology_ids`) and its prompt gains a `## TAUTOLOGICAL ASSERTIONS` section
386	  instructing it to re-author each so the tagged assertion FAILS at the merge-base baseline
387	  (reverting the change's WIRING file must break it), with the per-SPEC negctl diagnosis.
388	- **Build's charter is relaxed for flagged tautologies only.** A gate-flagged tautological SPEC is
389	  explicitly re-authorable; every other acceptance assertion remains protected by the don't-weaken rule.
390	- **No gaming, by construction.** The mechanical negative-control (Level 2 above) re-runs on the next
391	  iteration and rejects a still-tautological result; the cycle budget applies (`max_iterations` -> `rc=8`) **(superseded 2026-10-08 by ADR-054 §4 / #1850 — now rc 1 + `_CYCLE_LAST_OUTCOME=failed`)**.

393	The generic `route_target` carrier + the `build_test_cycle` `route_back` edge are **retained but
394	dormant** (no failure class currently sets `route_target`), ready for any genuinely design-rooted

416	## Amendment (#1660, 2026-08-01) — the bound only binds if it escalates to KILL
417	
418	The #1188 amendment above says each SPEC test runs "under `timeout ${ZBUILD_NEGCTL_TIMEOUT}`" and
419	enumerates rc 124/143. That description was accurate and the mechanism was still unsound: plain
420	`timeout` sends **TERM only**, so a child that traps or ignores TERM outruns its bound entirely.
421	
422	This is not hypothetical for *this* gate specifically. The negative control runs the declared TESTFILE
423	at the **merge-base**, where the defect under test is present by construction — so any issue whose
424	subject is signal handling has a baseline that can defeat the gate's own TERM. #1611 was exactly that
425	(a test harness whose TERM trap cleaned up and fell through), and it hung run `20260731204401-66454`
426	for 9h22m.
427	
428	`_negctl_run` / `_reachability_run` / `run-tests.sh` now bound each run with `-k <grace>`
429	(`ZBUILD_NEGCTL_KILL_GRACE` / `ZBUILD_TEST_KILL_GRACE`, default 10s), escalating to SIGKILL after the
430	grace. Worst-case per-run wall clock becomes `timeout + grace`.
431	
432	Two things make that safe, and both are load-bearing:
433	
434	- **rc 137 joins 124/143 as an infrastructure timeout.** Adding `-k` *without* this would be worse
435	  than the hang it replaces: the escalated exit would fall through to the ordinary control comparison
436	  and be reported as `tautology` / `not_passing_at_head` — a silently wrong verdict condemning a
437	  correct change. A hang at least announces itself. (rc 137 is also an external OOM kill; both mean
438	  the run's true pass/fail is unknown, which is the same INFRA disposition either way.)
439	- **`-k` support is probed, not assumed.** A `timeout` lacking the flag exits 125 on it, which is
440	  likewise not a timeout rc — every bounded run would be condemned rather than run. Support is
441	  verified once per process; a binary without it degrades to the old TERM-only bound.
442	
443	Both gates build the bound through one helper, `_acceptance_timeout_prefix` (`acceptance-block.sh`),
444	which also resolves `gtimeout` — previously only `run-tests.sh` did, leaving the acceptance gates
445	effectively unbounded on a macOS host with GNU coreutils but no POSIX `timeout`.

447	## Amendment (#1686, 2026-08-03) — wiring_not_on_path: distinct class + first live route_target activation
448	
449	**Problem.** When a declared WIRING target was absent from `git diff --name-only` (the file exists but
450	was not touched by this commit), `acceptance_reachability_check` still ran the full worktree flip-
451	detection. Since the target was never changed, baseline == HEAD for it, so no testfile could flip and
452	the result was `REACHABILITY FAIL inert_wiring`. That is the wrong class: `inert_wiring` means the
453	target IS in the diff but the suite fails to exercise it (a build-fixable test gap); here the author
454	named a file unrelated to this commit, which only design can correct.
455	
456	**Fix.**
457	
458	1. **`scripts/lib/acceptance-reachability.sh`** — before creating each target's worktree, check
459	   whether the target appears in `changed_files` (leading `./` normalised on both sides). If absent,
460	   emit `REACHABILITY FAIL wiring_not_on_path <target>`, set `rc=1`, and `continue`, skipping the
461	   expensive revert run. An empty `changed_files` with `head != base` means the `git diff` call
462	   failed (shallow clone, unresolvable base) and fails closed as `REACHABILITY ERROR diff_failed` —
463	   without that guard every target would read as off-diff and rewind every run to design.
464	
465	2. **`plugins/agent/spec-acceptance/plugin.sh`** — parse the new line in the Level-3 loop;
466	   accumulate `wiring_not_on_path:<target>` in `failures[]`; emit
467	   `acceptance.gate.wiring_not_on_path`. Classify `wiring_not_on_path:*` as **`recoverable`**
468	   (same row as `inert_wiring:*` and `tautology:*`). After classifying, scan `failures[]` for
469	   `wiring_not_on_path:*` and set `route_target="design"` — the **first live activation** of the
470	   dormant carrier that #1583 retained. The gate-aggregator rolls this up to `verdict=route_design`,

486	## Amendment (#1684, 2026-08-04) — the summary states what each SPEC claims and what was asserted, and it persists
487	
488	The concise operator summary above (#1211) reports a verdict per SPEC id and nothing about *what was
489	tested*. `NEGCTL PASS SPEC-2` asserts that some tagged assertion failed at the baseline and passes at
490	HEAD — not that the assertion has anything to do with what SPEC-2 claims. On run
491	`20260801225757-5482` it did not: design's `SPEC-2[change]` described a SIGTERM trap path, build
492	tagged an unrelated "killed tier prints ABORTED" assertion with the same id, and every mechanical
493	check was satisfied while the riskiest code in the change shipped with zero coverage.
494	
495	That gap is not mechanically decidable in general (see #1670, #1675, #1691 for the cases where it
496	partly is). This amendment makes it **visible** instead, and costs one rendering change plus one
497	artifact write.
498	
499	**1. Each per-SPEC line carries the design's claim and the asserted label, on their own lines.**
500	
501	```
502	NEGCTL PASS SPEC-2
503	      design : SIGTERM to the --tier all orchestrator … exits non-zero (INT/TERM trap path)
504	      asserts: assert_eq "[SPEC-2] killed mutation tier → 'mutation: ABORTED' on stderr" …
505	```
506	
507	The verdict token remains the leading content of its own line, so existing parsers and the
508	one-line-per-SPEC count are unaffected. Both strings are truncated at 100 chars with `…` — the
509	earlier 60 cut away the clause that distinguishes one SPEC from another, which is the only reason to
510	print it. Absent values render as `<no description>` / `<none found>`, never as a blank gap.
511	
512	**2. The label is the first line that INVOKES an assertion helper, not the first textual match.**
513	These testfiles routinely carry `[SPEC-n]` as fixture text — tests-of-the-gate write sandbox repos
514	whose bodies contain tags. Taking the first match reported a label that was never asserted, which is
515	worse than reporting nothing because it reads as confirmation. Two passes: assertion-shaped lines
516	across all declared testfiles first, any tagged line only as fallback.
517	
518	*Residual:* SPEC ids are file-global, so a testfile carrying the same id for a **different** design's
519	SPEC can still win pass 1. Not solvable without per-design id namespacing — tracked in #1691.
520	
521	**3. The summary is written to `artifacts/acceptance-summary.txt`.** `_ag_emit_operator_summary`
522	writes to a terminal fd and is io-gated on the stage having a `stdout` destination: on a file-only
523	install it produces nothing, and when it does fire it survives only as long as the scrollback. The
524	review lenses and any post-hoc audit of a finished run read artifacts. Without the file the
525	design-vs-assertion pairing is visible to nobody once the run ends — which is precisely when someone
526	goes looking for why a green run shipped an untested requirement.

528	## Amendment (#1670, 2026-08-04) — guard SPECs: inverted baseline check replaces SKIP
529	
530	> **Superseded by ADR-069 (#2304 part B, 2026-10-05).** `[guard]` and every guard path are gone: a done requirement (`[done]`, which the old `[guard]` reads as) and a no-code one are not run against the old code at all (`NEGCTL SKIP <id> already_done | no_code`). The text below is kept as history.
531	
532	**Problem.** `[guard]` SPECs were verified by one thing only: an assertion carrying the label exists.
533	The negative control was skipped outright (`NEGCTL SKIP guard_spec`), so nothing connected the SPEC's
534	English text to what its assertion actually asserted. Run `20260801085257-41853` shipped the exact
535	inversion this permits: design wrote *"`cleanup` without `--worktrees` does **not** reclaim
536	worktrees"*, build implemented the opposite and tagged an assertion agreeing with its own
537	implementation. All eight gate checks passed, 552 tests were green, six review lenses missed it.
538	
539	**Decision.** An invariant holds at the merge-base *by definition*. So run the same baseline harness
540	`[change]` SPECs already use and flip the expectation, rather than skipping:
541	
542	| SPEC class | expectation at the merge-base |
543	|---|---|
544	| `[change]` | the tagged assertion must **FAIL** there |
545	| `[guard]`  | the tagged assertion must **PASS** there |
546	
547	A guard assertion that fails at baseline is not a guard — it is a mislabelled `[change]`, or an
548	assertion inverted relative to its own SPEC text. Both are what the gate exists to catch.
549	
550	**Emission** (SPEC id leads every token, as on the `[change]` lines, so the #1684 summary enrichment
551	and the plugin's generic `NEGCTL FAIL <spec_id> <reason>` parser need no special-casing):
552	
553	- `NEGCTL PASS <spec_id> guard_spec` — invariant holds at baseline → gate OK
554	- `NEGCTL FAIL <spec_id> guard_regressed` — fails at baseline → gate fails
555	- `NEGCTL ERROR timeout:<spec_id>` / `harness:<spec_id>` — advisory, non-blocking
556	- `NEGCTL SKIP <spec_id> guard_untested` — no tagged assertion → nothing to measure
557	
558	**Two failure modes are NOT violations, and conflating them would make guards unlandable.**
559	
560	*The baseline run never reached an assertion.* A guard whose test depends on something the change
561	introduces cannot execute at the merge-base, and its rc is then evidence of nothing. Two
562	repo-agnostic signals separate this from a real assertion failure: a `bash -n` preflight on the
563	baseline copy (unparseable there), and the POSIX "could not execute" rc classes 126/127. Both yield
564	`NEGCTL ERROR harness:<spec_id>` → advisory. The check is skipped when a custom
565	`ZBUILD_ACCEPTANCE_RUN_CMD` is configured (#1478), so non-bash runners behave as before.
566	
567	*The guard carries no tagged assertion.* #1255 exempts `[guard]` SPECs from the design-gate's
568	tag-coverage rule, so an untagged guard is **legal input here**. Failing it would deadlock the
569	pipeline outright: the design-gate admits the design, this gate halts the cycle, and no rewind edge
570	exists for the class. It skips, exactly as before this amendment. The residual — a guard nobody wrote
571	an assertion for is unverified — is the tradeoff #1255 already accepted, tracked in #1683.
572	
573	**Disposition is `recoverable`, not terminal.** A guard assertion that contradicts its SPEC is the
574	same "weak test" symptom as tautology, and #1583 settled that class: route it to build with the
575	negctl diagnosis and let build re-author the assertion (build has owned assertion bodies since
576	#1477). Terminal would strand it — there is no `route_target` for this class, so the run could only
577	die at `max_iterations`.
578	
579	**Backward compatibility.** The `NEGCTL SKIP` reason tokens `no_impl_delta` and `no_prod_delta` are
580	unchanged (their *line shape* changed in the #1715 amendment below, which landed after this one).
581	`NEGCTL SKIP guard_spec` is no longer emitted; its enrichment arm in the plugin is removed
582	with it (noted on #1715, which documents that surface).
583	
584	## Amendment (#1715, 2026-08-05) — whole-run skips name their SPECs; timeout lines are enriched
585	
586	**Problem.** #1684 gave every `NEGCTL PASS|FAIL|SKIP <spec_id>` line the design's SPEC text and the
587	label of the assertion that ran. Two emission paths carried a SPEC id, or should have, and still
588	rendered bare:
589	
590	1. `NEGCTL ERROR timeout:<spec_id>` names its SPEC inside the detail token, after a colon rather than
591	   as a standalone word, so the enrichment regex never captured it. A SPEC whose negative control
592	   *timed out* is the one case where the gate could form no opinion at all — and it was the one case
593	   that printed nothing but an id.
594	2. `NEGCTL SKIP no_impl_delta` / `no_prod_delta` were emitted once for the whole run, before the
595	   per-SPEC loop, naming no SPEC. On any test-only diff the entire contract summary was one line, and
596	   the roster of SPECs that went unverified was invisible.
597	
598	The skip reasons are legitimate; the point is not to fail them. *"We verified nothing"* and *"we
599	verified nothing, and here is the list of what we did not verify"* are different operator messages,
600	and only the second is actionable.
601	
602	**Decision.**
603	
604	- Whole-run skips emit one `NEGCTL SKIP <spec_id> <reason>` per declared SPEC. The reason is
605	  run-wide; the roster is not. SPEC-id-first matches the convention the #1670 amendment above already
606	  adopted for `guard_untested` / `guard_regressed`, so the #1684 enrichment regex matches with no new
607	  branch and the classifier's existing `NEGCTL SKIP *` no-op arm is unchanged.
608	- **The bare `NEGCTL SKIP <reason>` line is retained as a fallback** when the SPEC roster cannot be
609	  read. Emitting nothing would turn the skip into silence, which reads identically to the check never
610	  having run — a strictly worse signal than the bare line this amendment replaces.
611	- Enrichment gains one arm for `^NEGCTL ERROR timeout:(SPEC-[0-9]+)`, extracting the id from the
612	  detail token.
613	
614	Both are rendering changes: the gate `verdict` and `failures[]` are unaffected in all three cases.
615	
616	**Not covered.** `REACHABILITY SKIP no_impl_delta` (Level 3) still emits one bare line naming no
617	WIRING target — the same defect at the other level. Tracked separately.
618	## Amendment (#1711, 2026-08-05) — inert_wiring iter≥2 escalation: second-measurement closes the #1664 shape
619	
620	**Problem.** Amendment #1686 separates *"WIRING target not in this change's diff"*
621	(`wiring_not_on_path` → routes immediately to design) from *"WIRING target in diff but no test
622	flips"* (`inert_wiring` → recoverable, build-fixable). It does **not** separate
623	*"untested but testable"* from *"untestable"*. #1664 (run `20260801225808-15285`) is the latter: a
624	CI-config change declared `WIRING: .github/workflows/test.yml`, which **was** in PR #1680's diff
625	(`+9/-2`), so it lands on `inert_wiring` — build-fixable — even though no shell testfile can load
626	workflow YAML. Build exhausted `max_iterations` writing static greps that the issue had explicitly
627	forbidden.
628	
629	**Two static predicates were considered and rejected.**
630	
631	1. *File-extension heuristic* — reject YAML/JSON paths as non-sourceable. Encodes target-language
632	   knowledge ADR-049 forbids; a `.yaml` test harness is a legal TESTFILE.
633	2. *Load-attempt probe* — `source` or `bash -n` each WIRING target before the revert loop. A shell
634	   that cannot parse the target would report an error; the gate would classify it differently.
635	   Rejected: this is still target-knowledge (assumes bash is the only runner) and breaks the
636	   `ZBUILD_ACCEPTANCE_RUN_CMD` seam.
637	3. *Target not in this change's diff* — treat a WIRING target absent from the diff as unfixable by
638	   build. Rejected because it does not fire on the motivating case at all: PR #1680 changed
639	   `.github/workflows/test.yml` (`+9/-2`), so the #1664 target **is** in the diff and still lands on
640	   `inert_wiring`. This predicate is already implemented, correctly, as the separate
641	   `wiring_not_on_path` class (Amendment #1686) — a narrower design error, not this one.
642	4. *No declared TESTFILE references the target* — the prescription in #1686's original body, built as
643	   PR #1697. Rejected by execution: it breaks R2 in
644	   `tests/integration/acceptance-gate-reachability-test.sh`, the #956 guard, where `inert-wiring.sh`
645	   is a bash stub no test references. A testfile *could* source it, so `inert_wiring` (build-fixable)
646	   is the correct verdict there. R2 and the #1664 shape are statically identical — "a file in the
647	   repo that no test mentions" — so any predicate that routes one routes both.
648	
649	Predicates 3 and 4 are recorded here because each was attempted and shipped as a non-fix; they should
650	not be re-attempted. They fail in opposite directions on the two cases, which is the tell that the
651	distinction is not statically recoverable at all.
652	
653	No static predicate at design time separates *"untested because build hasn't written the assertion
654	yet"* from *"untested because the target is structurally unloadable"*; they are byte-identical to any
655	inspection of the repository.
656	
657	**Decision — second measurement rather than a better guess.** Separate the cases by observation, not
658	prediction: let `inert_wiring` stand on the first iteration so build gets a genuine attempt. If the
659	same target is still inert on a second (or later) iteration, build has already had its chance; design
660	must correct the WIRING declaration (`WIRING: none`, or a different load-bearing file).
661	
662	**Mechanism.** In `plugins/agent/spec-acceptance/plugin.sh`, after the `wiring_not_on_path` scan,
663	add an iteration guard: when `route_target` is not already set AND `${ZBUILD_CYCLE_ITER:-1} ≥ 2`
664	AND any failure is `inert_wiring:*`, set `route_target="design"` and emit
665	`acceptance.gate.inert_wiring_escalated`. `ZBUILD_CYCLE_ITER` is exported by the cycle orchestrator
666	(`core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh`) — no engine or template plumbing is required.
667	
668	**Disposition stays `recoverable`.** A `terminal` disposition halts `build_test_cycle` before the
669	gate-aggregator can read `route_target` and emit `route_design`. The same rationale governs
670	`wiring_not_on_path` (Amendment #1686): `recoverable` lets the aggregator run, read
671	`route_target=design`, and produce `verdict=route_design` — which the cycle runner's `route_back`
672	guard matches, rewinding to `design_verify_cycle`. The global route_back budget bounds ping-pong.
673	
674	**First attempt is preserved.** iter=1 (ZBUILD_CYCLE_ITER unset or 1): `inert_wiring` is emitted
675	with no `route_target` — the failure is recoverable and build re-iterates normally. iter≥2: the same
676	still-inert target is now routed to design. This asymmetry is intentional: a build-fixable gap that
677	build genuinely closes in one iteration never reaches the escalation guard.
678	
679	**Scope.** The escalation is implemented only for `inert_wiring:*`. The same guard pattern applies to
680	`tautology:*` and `untagged_spec:*` in principle, but the acceptance criteria only test
681	`inert_wiring`; generalisation is a follow-up if the pipeline owner wants it.

683	## Amendment (#1777, 2026-08-24) — the guard check runs at the design-gate too, and `guard_regressed` routes to design
684	
685	> **Superseded by ADR-069 (#2304 part B, 2026-10-05).** `[guard]` and every guard path are gone: a done requirement (`[done]`, which the old `[guard]` reads as) and a no-code one are not run against the old code at all (`NEGCTL SKIP <id> already_done | no_code`). 687	**Problem.** ADR-036 §"Amendment (#1670)" made a `[guard]` SPEC's assertion answerable at the
688	merge-base, and the gate has been catching mislabels correctly ever since. It catches them in the
689	wrong *place*. The check lives at the post-build acceptance gate, so a two-word error — `[guard]`
690	where the author meant `[change]` — is not visible until build has spent its entire iteration
691	budget on the design. #1789 lost 5 iterations and 2h06m; #1809 lost 2 more (~1h39m and ~1h05m) and
692	was aborted at iteration 3 of 5. Both wanted the same two-word fix.

694	Worse, the rewind that exists for exactly this could not deliver it. `simple.yaml` declares
695	`route_back: {to: design_verify_cycle, when: gate-aggregator.verdict == route_design}`, but
696	`guard_regressed` set **no** `route_target`, so the gate-aggregator's #1757 partition put it in
697	`residual[]` and wrote it to the BUILD-facing `gate-feedback.md`. On #1809 the winning
698	`route_target` came from shape-floor, so `design-feedback.md` — the payload the rewind carries —
699	named only shape-floor. Design re-authored nothing, build re-ran, the same guard failed again.
700	
701	**Decision.**
702	
703	1. **`guard_regressed` is design-rooted.** `spec-acceptance` sets `route_target=design` for it,
704	   alongside `wiring_not_on_path` (#1583) and escalated `inert_wiring` (#1711). Build cannot fix a
705	   mislabelled tag; the correction is the tag or the assertion, and both live in the design.
706	   Disposition stays `recoverable` — `terminal` would halt the cycle before the aggregator reads
707	   `route_target`, the same rationale as #1686/#1711.
708	
709	2. **The design-gate gains C6**, applying the §"Amendment (#1670)" rule one stage earlier via
710	   `acceptance_negctl_guard_precheck`. The per-SPEC resolution and the ✓/✗ discrimination (#1737)
711	   are *extracted*, not reimplemented — `_negctl_guard_resolve_tfs` and `_negctl_guard_verdict` are
712	   shared by both callers, so the two gates cannot come to disagree about the same design.
713	
714	**What C6 does NOT do, stated plainly.** It cannot save the *first* build cycle. At the first
715	design pass the branch has no commits, so the merge-base IS HEAD and there is nothing to revert to;
716	more fundamentally the assertion does not exist yet, because since #1477 BUILD authors every
717	assertion body. C6 earns its keep on the **rewind** — after `route_design` sends the run back, it

724	acceptance gate remains the authority.

732	entirely when a design declares no `[guard]` SPEC, so a guard-less design's artifact shape is
733	unchanged.
734	
735	**Unchanged.** Level-2 at the acceptance gate is untouched — C6 is an earlier net, not a
736	replacement. `tautology` still carries no `route_target` and still reaches build (#1583).

738	## Amendment (#2022, 2026-09-01) — assertion authorship leaves build
739	
740	**Problem.** This ADR's own premise (:318, :347) is that build must not touch
741	acceptance assertions, *"else it games the gate"*, because design authored them.
742	That premise stopped holding at **#1477** — and not by decision. #1477 removed a
743	design-stage **bash stub-writer** as a target-agnosticism leak (a bash stub is
744	nonsense in a pytest or Rust repo); build inherited assertion ownership as a side
745	effect, and later amendments built on it (#1583 routes tautologies to build to
746	re-author; #1670 does the same for guard inversions).
747	
748	The consequence is **correlated authorship**: build writes the code and the
749	assertion from one reading of the SPEC, so the two agree by construction and no
750	check comparing them can catch a misreading. Two runs shipped exactly that —
751	run `20260801085257-41853` (recorded in the #1670 amendment above) and #1836's
752	SPEC-7, where the assertion checked the literal opposite of its SPEC and passed
753	all three levels honestly.
754	
755	Build's prompt was **followed** in both cases: it said *"correct the assertion so
756	that it does"* test its SPEC. Build was the one judging whether it did.
757	
758	**Decision.** Assertion authorship moves to a `test_author` role, upstream of
759	build:
760	
761	| Link | Owner | How |
762	|---|---|---|
763	| spec → assertion | `test-author` (authors), QA (judges — future) | — |
764	| assertion → implementation | `test` stage | execution |
765	| assertion is not tautological | Level 2 | experiment |
766	| wiring is load-bearing | Level 3 | experiment |
767	| assertions unmodified by build | `assertion-integrity` | digest comparison |
768	
769	`test-author` leads `build_test_cycle` and sees the SPEC text and the target
770	testfile paths — never the diff. It is an **agent authoring in the target's own
771	language**, never a mechanical stub-writer: #1477's constraint is respected, and
772	that is why authorship returns to a model stage rather than to design.
773	
774	**The boundary is enforced, not requested.** #1919 P5 measured that
775	`permissions.deny` is honoured in `Edit(...)` form; the spawn now denies build
776	Edit on the declared TESTFILES, derived by ROLE rather than by stage id. P5 also
777	measured that a `Write(...)` rule matches nothing, so prevention is incomplete by
778	construction — `assertion-integrity` compares the files against the digests the
779	author recorded and fails the cycle on a difference. It reads what changed on
780	disk, never what a prompt asked for.
781	
782	**What this retires.** #1583's tautology feed to build and its re-author mandate
783	(`build/lib/prompt.sh:191`, `_build_read_tautology_ids`). The same
784	`prior_acceptance_feedback.txt` path now carries the finding to `test-author`.
785	Levels 1–3 are unchanged: they are experiments, and no reading replaces them.
