835	
836	The gate now does for `tautology:*` what #2097 did for `not_passing_at_head`: on
837	`ZBUILD_CYCLE_ITER ≥ 2` it sets `fault=specification` and emits
838	`acceptance.gate.tautology_escalated spec=<id> iter=<n>`; the disposition stays
839	`recoverable`. The design prompt's classification rule now says to check the tree before
840	tagging `[change]` — behaviour that already exists at the merge-base is a `[guard]` — and
841	the route-back replay offers re-tagging as the honest resolution, not only re-authoring.
842	*(Superseded by ADR-069: there is no relabel offer. A requirement the code already meets
843	is `[done]` with evidence the design-gate checks; otherwise design rewrites it so its test
844	fails on the old code.)*
845	This is the sentence above ("the change-vs-guard classification … is design-side") made
846	operational. Verification: `acceptance-gate-tautology-escalation-test.sh` (iter 1 no fault;
847	iter 2 fault + event), `design-prior-gate-feedback-test.sh` T1 (#2157 assertions).
848	
849	## Amendment (#2161, 2026-09-20) — `severity` carries the cycle-policy word; `disposition` is ADR-054's
850	
851	The gate wrote `result_contract: 2` while filling `disposition` with ADR-021's member
852	vocabulary — `none` on a pass, `recoverable`/`advisory`/`terminal` on a failure — and the
853	no-failures branch wrote no `reason`. ADR-054's reader requires `verdict`/`disposition`/`reason`
854	and a `disposition` from its closed set; on a pass (rc 0) it refused the result, and #1840 run 6
855	ended `failed/blocked` fifteen seconds after the gate had verified all 19 SPECs. The failure
856	paths carried the same wrong words and were only ever tolerated because rc≠0 skips the reader.
857	
858	Now: `disposition` is `complete` on every path where the gate reached a conclusion (the
859	verdict says what it concluded); `reason` is always written (a pass says "all N SPEC(s)
860	verified"); and the cycle-policy word from `_ag_classify_disposition` is `severity`
861	(`none|recoverable|advisory|terminal`, the #1959/#2129 vocabulary and its lint unchanged).
862	`_cycle_member_terminal_failure` halts on `severity == terminal` and the gate-aggregator
863	demotes `severity == advisory`, both reading `disposition` as the fallback for v1-shaped
864	results. Verification: `tests/integration/acceptance-gate-v2-reader-test.sh` (the real gate's
865	pass, fail, precondition-unmet and malformed results through `runner_read_stage_verdict` with
866	rc 0 — red before: `missing_field:reason`, `unknown_disposition:recoverable`), and
867	`gate-v2-contract-test.sh` SPEC-15 (every mechanical gate's pass result through the reader).
868	
869	## Amendment (2026-09-28): a tag carries its issue — `[#<issue>/SPEC-n]`
870	
871	SPEC numbers restart with every design, so a bare `[SPEC-3]` never said WHICH
872	issue's SPEC-3 it was. That stayed harmless while each issue's assertions lived
873	in its own files; it broke when a design listed a SHARED test. #1845's design
874	named `tests/integration/deployed-template-e2e-test.sh`, and test-author's
875	stale-tag step (#2174) read every tag whose number was not in #1845's contract
876	as stale — stripping #1328's `[SPEC-1..10]` from 26 assertions.
877	
878	**Decision — add, never overlap.**
879	- Under an issue, the tag is `[#<issue>/SPEC-n]` (e.g. `[#1845/SPEC-3]`).
880	  `acceptance_spec_tag` (`scripts/lib/acceptance-block.sh`) is the one place that
881	  builds it; every reader — coverage, the negative control, reachability, label
882	  lookup — matches that exact string. `ZBUILD_ISSUE` (exported by the runner)
883	  supplies the number; with no issue (a `--goal` run) the tag is the bare legacy
884	  `[SPEC-n]`.
885	- An existing `[SPEC-n]` keeps its meaning and is never rewritten. The two forms
886	  cannot match each other: `\[SPEC-[0-9]+\]` does not match a new tag, and no
887	  reader looks for a bare tag under an issue.
888	- test-author's stale-tag step considers only THIS issue's tags. A bare tag or
889	  another issue's tag belongs to other work and is never touched. The prompts
890	  (test-author, build, design) show the literal tag to write.
891	
892	**Cost, stated.** An issue that already has an in-flight work branch written
893	under bare tags gets new issue tags on its next run; its old bare tags stay (they
894	are no longer this run's to remove) and count for nothing.
895	
896	Verification: `tests/unit/issue-scoped-spec-tags-test.sh` (T1–T6).
897	
898	## Amendment (2026-09-28): a signal is not a timeout
899	
900	The negative control classed exit codes 124, 137 and 143 as "timed out" —
901	infrastructure, advisory, owned by nobody. Those codes are OS conventions, not
902	zBuild's: GNU `timeout` exits **124** when its own timer fires (137 if its `-k`
903	kill-after lands), while **143** is 128+15 — "a SIGTERM killed it", sent by
904	anyone. **#1847 run 20260928144733-57620**: a TESTFILE stubbed the model call as
905	`kill -TERM "$$"`, died at the merge-base after ~1s, and every SPEC after that
906	point read `negctl_error:timeout` under a 60s timer that never fired.
907	
908	- **Timeout** is now only the timer's own codes: 124, and 137 when the kill-after
909	  is in use.
910	- **`killed_by_signal`** (new, recoverable): the run ended on a signal (128+N)
911	  the timer did not send, and printed no ✓/✗ for this SPEC. On both the
912	  `[change]` and `[guard]` paths. Its reason names the usual cause — a test that
913	  signals its own process where no handler exists — and the fix: signal a child.
914	- A verdict the file printed **before** dying is still evidence and is used as
915	  it stands.
916	- A **SIGKILL** (137) the timer did not send is `NEGCTL ERROR sigkill:` —
917	  infrastructure. Nothing in a test normally sends SIGKILL; the usual sender is
918	  the OOM killer, and "signal a child" would be the wrong advice (review #2220).
919	
920	Verification: `tests/unit/acceptance-negctl-signal-test.sh` (S1–S6).
921	
922	### Amendment (2026-09-29, #2234) — not measured is never "failed"
923	
924	> **Superseded by ADR-069 (#2304 part B, 2026-10-05).** `[guard]` and every guard path are gone: a done requirement (`[done]`, which the old `[guard]` reads as) and a no-code one are not run against the old code at all (`NEGCTL SKIP <id> already_done | no_code`). The text below is kept as history.
925	
926	The negative control runs HEAD's TESTFILE against the merge-base code (and again at HEAD). On #1835 an earlier `[change]` step in that file called a function that returns non-zero before the change, bare under `set -e`, so the file exited there. Every assertion after that point never ran. The gate read "no verdict for SPEC-18" as "SPEC-18 fails at the merge-base". It reported `guard_regressed`, declared a specification fault, and rewound design three times to relabel a guard that held. Verified: at the merge-base the template still wins, as SPEC-18 says.
927	
928	**The rule.** Only an assertion's **own** printed verdict is evidence about it. When there is none, the file's output says which of two cases it is.
929	
930	- **Unreached.** The file printed ✓/✗ verdicts for **other** SPECs of this contract and none for this one, so it stopped before this assertion ran. The line names the last SPEC that printed (`after=SPEC-n`). This holds in any language, because it reads the contract's own tag shape. Unreached is the file's or the code's to fix, **never design's**:
931	  - `guard_unreached`: a `[guard]` at the merge-base;
932	  - `unreached_at_base`: a `[change]` at the merge-base. Its negative control is unproven; before this it was accepted as valid;
933	  - `unreached_at_head`: a `[change]` on the new code. It is not escalated to design, unlike `not_passing_at_head`.
934	- **A 126/127 exit inside a file that printed other verdicts** is a command the change introduces, missing at the merge-base: the file executed and stopped there. It is unreached, not `harness`.
935	- **Unverified (`guard_unverified`).** The file printed no verdicts at all: a bare check (#1658), or a framework that does not print the contract's ✓/✗ lines. Its rc cannot tell "checked and failed" from "died first".
936	  - It still **fails** the gate. #2129's reason for not skipping it stands; NC-F7 must not go inert.
937	  - It is not called a regression. On the first round the finding goes to the testfile's owner. It escalates to a specification fault only if it is still unverified on round 2 (`acceptance.gate.guard_unverified_escalated`).
938	- **Unchanged:** a guard that prints its **own** ✗ at the merge-base is still `guard_regressed`, a specification fault on round 1.
939	- **`about`:** when every finding is about a testfile that did not measure its SPEC (`guard_unreached`, `unreached_at_base`, `guard_unverified`), the result's `about` names the testfile(s), so the engine frames the finding for the stage that wrote them (#2180).
940	- **The design-gate precheck fails open on both:** `GUARD SKIP <spec> guard_unreached|guard_unverified`.
941	
942	Why design is the last resort: rewinding design on a guess re-authors a correct design, and the same failure returns every round (#1835: three rounds, 6h). Sending a real design fault to build or test-author first costs one round, and the round-2 escalation still reaches design.
943	
944	Verification: `tests/unit/acceptance-negctl-unreached-test.sh` (U1–U10).
945	
946	### Amendment (2026-09-30, #2244, #2243) — a broken guard test, and existing checks the change makes wrong
947	
948	> **Partly superseded by ADR-069 (#2304 part B, 2026-10-05).** The `guard_test_broken` half (#2244) went with `[guard]`; the `supersedes` half (#2243) stands.
949	
950	- **`guard_test_broken` (#2244).** A `[guard]`'s own check prints ✗ at the merge-base. The gate now also runs it at HEAD, and if it prints ✗ there too, the check itself is broken: it fails whatever the code does.
951	  - It is recoverable, not a specification fault.
952	  - The finding is `about` the testfile.
953	  - The design-gate precheck fails open on it.
954	  - #1838: `grep -qF "- x"` (read as an option) failed on both sides and was blamed on design as a mislabel.
955	- **`supersedes` (#2243).** Design may list existing checks the change makes wrong, in a separate fenced block: `path [TAG]: why`.
956	  - Updating them to the new behaviour is test-author's job, and those files join its context paths. Only listed tags become editable.
957	  - Build stays read-only on testfiles.
958	  - #1842: no stage could make the edit, so build evaded an old grep.
959	
960	Verification: `tests/unit/test-author-supersedes-test.sh` (`tests/unit/acceptance-negctl-guard-broken-test.sh` was deleted with `[guard]`, #2304).
961	
962	### Amendment (2026-10-05, #2300) — plugin tests are tests for the test-only skip
963	
964	The negative control skips with `no_prod_delta` when every changed path is a test, because there is no old code to run the tests against. It counted a path as a test only when it started with `tests/`. Plugin tests live under `plugins/<kind>/<id>/tests/`, so #2035 (plugin tests, `tests/unit/` and an ADR) was judged as a code change, and each test file "passed on the old code".
965	
966	- **The rule.** A path counts as a test path when it starts with `tests/` **or** matches `plugins/<kind>/<id>/tests/`. A change made only of such paths skips with `no_prod_delta`.
967	- **Guard.** Any other path in the change, such as `plugins/<kind>/<id>/plugin.sh`, is production code, and the full control runs.
968	- Documentation paths are not test paths; this amendment does not change that.
969	
970	Verification: `tests/unit/acceptance-negctl-plugin-tests-test.sh` (P1 skip, P2 guard).
971	
972	### Amendment (2026-10-05, #2304) — code nobody claims fails the check (ADR-069)
973	
974	Requirements now carry a status (ADR-069 §1): `[code]`, `[no-code]` or `[done]`; the old `[change]` is read as code and `[guard]` as done. A new first check (ADR-069 §5) fails the acceptance check when the branch changes production code (anything except `tests/`, `plugins/<kind>/<id>/tests/`, `docs/` and `*.md`) and no requirement is code. The failure class is `unclaimed_code` (recoverable). The rest of this ADR's guard rules are replaced by ADR-069 in PR B of #2304.
975	
976	Verification: `tests/unit/acceptance-unclaimed-code-test.sh` (U1–U4).
977	
978	### Amendment (2026-10-05, #2304 part B) — the guard paths are removed (ADR-069 §3, §4)
979	
980	The negative control reads each requirement's status. A code requirement (`[code]`, the old `[change]`, or no tag) keeps the rule above: its test must fail on the old code and pass on the new. A done requirement (`[done]`, or an old `[guard]`) and a no-code one are not run: `NEGCTL SKIP <id> already_done` and `NEGCTL SKIP <id> no_code`. With no code requirement at all, no worktree is made. Tag coverage (Level 1) exempts the same two. Removed: the guard half of `acceptance-negctl.sh` (the baseline-only run, `guard_spec`, `guard_regressed`, `guard_unreached`, `guard_unverified`, `guard_test_broken`, `guard_untested`), the design-gate pre-check (#1777), the `acceptance.gate.guard_regressed` event and the guard failure classes. The per-SPEC log scan the guard arm shared with the code arm and reachability is now `_negctl_spec_log_check`. The pass reason counts the requirements checked on the old and new code, already done, and needing no code.
981	
982	Verification: `tests/unit/acceptance-negctl-status-test.sh` (N1–N5), `tests/unit/acceptance-coverage-test.sh` (C7, C9).
983
